why_trail.why: Two blockers, both in scripts/code_map/render.py. B1: loc() line 173 builds 'file:line' and is the ONLY position emitter -- render.py:306 (module index) already emits 'file, N lines' with no line number, so the handoff's claim that 306 does the same is wrong and 306 needs no change. loc() has exactly one call site, entity_page line 262. B2: run() lines 395-417 increments npages per write_text call. Key realisation: a set of distinct resolved path STRINGS would NOT fix this repo's real divergence, because Verdict.md vs verdict.md are distinct strings that collide only on a case-insensitive filesystem -- so pages must be counted from the files actually on disk. Test fixtures must force a collision or the assertion cannot fail; a class named INDEX collides with the module's own INDEX.md by exact path, which diverges on every platform, unlike the case collision which is invisible on Linux.

B1 landed at render.py loc() (now lines 171-188). One line of behaviour: head is the bare file path, no ':<line>'. The ', N lines' suffix and the path both survive, and a second test enforces that -- proved by mutating head to '' and watching it fail on all 3 pages. render.py:306, which the handoff said also emits a position, does NOT: it already emits 'file, N lines'. loc() has exactly one caller (entity_page). The stripped line number is not lost, only uncommitted: .code-map/statements.jsonl already carries per-statement {file,line,col} and is gitignored, so no new cache was needed or built.

B2 landed at render.py run(): the npages counter is gone from the write loop entirely and 'pages' is now sum(1 for _ in out.rglob('*.md')) at render.py:436 -- read off the tree, so it cannot disagree with the tree. Rejected the obvious alternative of deduplicating resolved path strings: Verdict.md and verdict.md are distinct strings and one file, so a set would still have reported 3636. The fixture had to force a collision or the assertion could not fail, and it uses a class named INDEX colliding with its own module's INDEX.md -- an exact-path collision that diverges on EVERY platform, unlike the real repo's case collision which is invisible on Linux. Out of scope but noted: 'entity_pages' in the same report still counts emit() calls and carries the identical defect.

Boundary verified. Full suite 1709 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed with PYTHONIOENCODING cleared -- exactly the 1706/2/0 baseline plus the 3 tests this pass adds. Real-repo figure moved 3636 -> 3635 against an unchanged on-disk 3635, with the Verdict page still lost, which is the stated correct outcome. One finding the handoff did not anticipate: a blunt position scan of the real tree still returns 2 hits, both from ONE authored docstring in tests/test_checklist_engine.py that names scripts/checklist_engine.py:449 in its own prose (echoed onto the entity page and its module index line). That is copied source text, not a renderer-emitted position, and it churns only when its own docstring changes -- but a reviewer grepping the committed map/ at gs will hit it, so it is recorded in the test docstring and reported up.

Committed b14ff3f with 15 explicit paths -- render.py, tests/test_code_map.py, this plan and its journal, the engine side-car, and the result. git add -A never used and map/ verified still untracked (git ls-files map = 0), so gate gs's staging is undisturbed. IMPLEMENTER_RESULT written with both mutation proofs at full output, the 3636->3635 figure against an unchanged on-disk 3635, the 1709/2/0 suite number, and three out-of-scope findings: entity_pages carries the identical uncountable-number defect and should go to g1 beside tc17; a blunt position grep of the committed tree returns 2 hits from one authored docstring, not renderer output; and the reference prototype still carries the old file:line header.
